cohort.body_name: Durham Public Schools Board of Education
cohort.label: Jul–Sep 2020 Board of Education (District B Vacancy)
cohort.transition_reason: Swearing-in of March 3, 2020 election winners Alexandra Valladares (At-Large, defeating incumbent Steve Unruhe) and Jovonia Lewis (Consolidated District A, succeeding retiring 16-year member Minnie Forte-Brown). Consolidated District B incumbent Xavier Cason won re-election in March 2020 but resigned in June 2020 prior to taking the new term to join the Durham Public Schools Foundation, leaving a 6-member board. Bettina Umstead elected Chair; Mike Lee elected Vice Chair.

example_votes.item_title: Approve Implementation of Six DPS Learning Centers with Prioritization and Health Metrics
example_votes.notes: Recorded 5-0-1 with Matt Sears abstaining; Board Attorney Rod Malone advised that an unexcused abstention technically counts as an affirmative vote (6-0 legally).

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session August 13, 2020 5:00 PM
conflicts.issue: DPS Learning Centers Safety Risks, COVID-19 Spread, and Health Metrics
conflicts.summary: While members recognized urgent equity needs for vulnerable families during Plan C, Matt Sears abstained and others sought strict health metrics before opening six in-person Learning Centers for 900 students.
conflicts.side_a_position: Proceed with launching six DPS Learning Centers on August 24/31 with vulnerable-student prioritization and built-in health metrics for opening and closing.
side_a_arguments: McKinney-Vento, foster, and free/reduced-lunch families urgently need safe supervised spaces, meals, and peer interaction during remote learning.
Embedding epidemiological metrics (inspired by Cambridge Public Schools and Duke/UNC advisors) creates clear guardrails for pausing if community spread worsens.
conflicts.side_b_position: Abstain over unresolved employee and student health risks given a 19% infection rate among school-age youth.
side_b_arguments: Calling the centers a 'guinea pig program,' Sears expressed lack of confidence that August 24/31 was the right or safe moment for employees and children despite strong equity arguments.
conflicts.resolution: Natalie Beyer's friendly amendment requiring health metrics was accepted and the motion passed 5-0-1, with Matt Sears abstaining (counted as an affirmative vote legally).

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session August 13, 2020 5:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Letter Urging Local PACs Not to Endorse in District B Vacancy Appointment
conflicts.summary: Board members split over sending a formal letter requesting Durham political action committees refrain from endorsing any of the 10 applicants for the vacant Consolidated District B seat.
conflicts.side_a_position: Encourage local PACs to refrain from endorsements so the six-member appointment process stays transparent and unmuddied.
side_a_arguments: Only six board members vote on the appointment, unlike public elections where endorsements inform voters.
PAC endorsements during a pandemic using virtual meetings could alienate members and replicate issues avoided when PACs refrained during Bettina Umstead's 2019 appointment.
conflicts.side_b_position: Do not issue the letter because an elected body asking PACs not to endorse is an improper overstep.
side_b_arguments: Feedback from PACs during the prior appointment process felt like the school board was overstepping its role by trying to shape independent PAC actions.
conflicts.resolution: Seeing no full board consensus, members agreed not to hold a vote on the letter, leaving individual board members free to sign or decline.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session   July 16, 2020  5:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Creating In-Person Safe Learning Pods/Childcare Under Plan C vs. Staff Safety and Certification
conflicts.summary: While board members united behind Plan C remote learning for the first nine weeks, they diverged over whether DPS should use classified staff or community pods to offer in-person learning spaces for vulnerable students.
conflicts.side_a_position: Pair Plan C remote learning with community-partnered safe spaces/learning stations to protect high-need students who lack safe environments at home.
side_a_arguments: Many low-income and vulnerable students face food insecurity, lack adult supervision, or risk domestic harm under full remote isolation.
Community partners and non-teaching staff or volunteers could help host safe spaces without forcing teachers into classrooms.
conflicts.side_b_position: Caution against relying on classified staff or creating in-person pods that replicate unsafe school exposures and lack certified instructional support.
side_b_arguments: In-person pods recreate the same COVID-19 transmission risks inside high-incidence communities, and classified staff are not certified for instruction.
Only 13% of teachers surveyed by DAE said they felt ready to return, and if flexibility existed, starting after Labor Day would give teachers preparation time.
conflicts.resolution: Board members voted unanimously 6-0 to adopt Plan C for the first nine weeks while directing administration to explore community-partnered safe spaces and bring back concrete health metrics.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session August 13, 2020 5:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Policy 9300 (Naming Facilities): Allowing Whole Schools to Be Named After Individuals
conflicts.summary: Natalie Beyer objected to draft Policy 9300 language allowing entire school facilities to be named after individuals deceased at least five years, while other members favored keeping the option.
conflicts.side_a_position: Prohibit naming entire schools after individuals altogether.
side_a_arguments: Schools named after people tend to be named after politicians, and prior naming processes (such as Lucas Middle School) proved contentious and difficult.
conflicts.side_b_position: Retain the option to name schools after deceased individuals (at least five years posthumous) when nominated by a sizable or recognizable community group.
side_b_arguments: Durham has rich local history and leadership worth honoring without artificially restricting future naming options.
conflicts.resolution: With Beyer noting she appeared to be the lone objector, administration kept the draft language to return for a full-board vote at the end-of-month meeting.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session August 13, 2020 5:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Federal Title IX Sexual Harassment Policy Waiver and Compliance Risk
conflicts.summary: Board members clashed over administration's request to waive second reading and immediately adopt new federal Title IX regulations taking effect August 14 despite weakened student protections.
conflicts.side_a_position: Refuse to adopt the weakened federal regulations without knowing the concrete penalty for noncompliance.
side_a_arguments: The Trump/DeVos rules raise the bar for pursuing sexual harassment claims, exclude off-campus incidents, and put students and staff at greater risk.
If noncompliance only brings administrative citation rather than loss of federal funding for students and teachers, Durham should stand against the rule.
conflicts.side_b_position: Seek a compliant interim legal path—such as a short-term placeholder resolution—while researching Attorney General Josh Stein's lawsuit and stronger local protections.
side_b_arguments: August 14 is a federal statutory deadline with compliance checks, and the district must avoid jeopardizing federal funds while preserving DPS's internal student-protection practices.
conflicts.resolution: The board tabled the item until after closed session, when Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni withdrew the request to waive second reading and deferred Title IX policies to the next board meeting.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Special Meeting   July 23, 2020  5:00 PM
conflicts.issue: Application Window Length and Interview Format for Consolidated District B Vacancy
conflicts.summary: Board members differed on whether to provide two or three weeks for District B applications and whether interviews should rely on prepared speeches or per-member live questions.
conflicts.side_a_position: Provide a longer application window (until August 17) and incorporate both individual member questions/spontaneous prompts and prepared speeches.
side_a_arguments: Xavier Cason's resignation surprised the community during summer and the COVID-19 pandemic, warranting extra outreach time.
Allowing each member to ask a question honors board diversity and reveals how candidates think on the fly.
conflicts.side_b_position: Keep a tighter two-week application cadence (August 10) and rely on a 7-10 minute prepared speech covering shared themes to prevent an overly long meeting.
side_b_arguments: Long gaps between filing, interviews, and selection invite excessive lobbying and protracted meetings if 10-13 candidates each answer six separate questions.
conflicts.resolution: Following compromise proposals from Alexandra Valladares and Jovonia Lewis, all six members verbally agreed to set the filing deadline for August 12, submit proposed questions to Chair Umstead by August 6 for thematic synthesis (blending prepared speeches with spontaneous prompts), review the pool on August 13, interview on August 20, and vote on August 27.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Organizational Meeting   July 7, 2020  8:30 AM
conflicts.issue: Frequency of July/August Reopening Meetings and August 17 Start Messaging
conflicts.summary: Natalie Beyer sought weekly Thursday board meetings through early August and objected to language assuming schools would reopen in person on August 17, while Dr. Mike Lee and Dr. Pascal Mubenga favored fewer fixed dates to give staff respite.
conflicts.side_a_position: Schedule weekly Thursday meetings (July 16, 23, 30, and August 6) and explicitly avoid messaging that schools will reopen in person on August 17.
side_a_arguments: Families and staff are hungry for weekly reopening updates, and current North Carolina COVID-19 conditions are unsafe for in-person school.
conflicts.side_b_position: Lock in July 16 and July 30 meetings while allowing staff vacation downtime and adding special-called meetings only if needed.
side_b_arguments: Central-office staff have been working nonstop on reopening plans and need brief downtime; referring to August 17 merely reflects the current state statutory calendar date pending Governor Cooper's guidance.
conflicts.resolution: The board unanimously adopted the 2020-21 calendar adding July 16 and July 30 while agreeing to call special interim meetings as state guidance evolved.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting   August 27,  2020  6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead presided over the August 27, 2020 Durham Public Schools Board of Education monthly meeting (with six seated members prior to filling the Consolidated District B vacancy), opening with a moment of silence after the police shooting of Jacob Blake and an update from Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga on remote learning, missing enrollment (779 students shy of projections), device/hotspot distribution, and DPS Learning Centers projecting up to $3.5 million in full-year net costs. Following unanimous approval of the agenda (6-0), June 25 and July 30 minutes (6-0), and consent agenda covering 6400/8000/9000 policies and the Waterford Learning contract (6-0), Dr. Mike Lee nominated Frederick Xavier Ravin III to fill the Consolidated District B seat vacated by Xavier Cason, which the board approved unanimously 6-0. The board then unanimously adopted second-reading edits to Policy 8000 (Fiscal Goals), principal student-transportation, and Community Use of Facilities (6-0); reluctantly adopted interim federal Title IX policies with a waiver of second reading while committing to restore stronger local student protections (6-0); adopted the Remote Work Policy on second reading (6-0); heard an update on 100% school participation in the Day One anti-bullying campaign; and approved the August 27 personnel report (6-0) after closed session.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Superintendent's Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the meeting to order (inadvertently saying July 30 before proceeding with August 27 business) and led a moment of silence for Jacob Blake and anti-racism commitment. Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga and staff reported on the second week of remote learning, 779 unconfirmed students prior to the 20th-day count, technology/hotspot deployment, and DPS Learning Centers projecting $97,826 in weekly net deficits ($3.5 million full year), prompting discussion of EC priority slots and SRO funding.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review, Approval of Minutes, and General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the agenda (6-0) and the June 25 and July 30, 2020 board minutes (6-0). Thirty public comments were read at one minute each covering virtual assessment timing, EC student supports under Plan C, technology login hurdles, and the Consolidated District B appointment.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously approved the consent agenda containing multiple policies in the 6400, 8000, and 9000 series as well as the Waterford Learning contract.

agenda_items.title: Appointment to Vacant Consolidated District B Seat
agenda_items.discussion_summary: To fill the Consolidated District B seat vacated by Xavier Cason in July, Dr. Mike Lee nominated Frederick Xavier Ravin III, and all six seated board members voted Aye by roll call. Board members praised the full candidate pool—including Dr. Fatima Sallie and Antonio Jones—and noted Ravin would be sworn in at the next work session.

agenda_items.title: Chief of Staff: Second-Reading Policies (8000, Student Transport, Facilities) and Interim Title IX Policies
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni presented revised second-reading policies—Policy 8000 (Fiscal Goals), principal emergency student transport (drafted by Matt Sears), and Community Use of Facilities removing 'private' to accommodate loosely affiliated parent groups—all passing 6-0. Giovanni and Legal Counsel Ken Soo then presented compromise interim Title IX policies complying with August 14 federal Department of Education rules while preparing local grievance alternatives; Natalie Beyer reluctantly moved adoption and waiver of second reading, passing 6-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Second-reading policies passed 6-0; Title IX policies passed 6-0

agenda_items.title: Operational/HR: Remote Work Policy (Second Reading)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented second-reading edits removing 'eligible employees' to focus on position eligibility and adding language in Section D1 committing to make every effort to provide alternative assignments, while noting a 25% employee fee discount at Learning Centers. Natalie Beyer moved and Dr. Mike Lee seconded adoption.

agenda_items.title: Day One Anti-Bullying Campaign Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy and Jamie Stroud reported 100% DPS school participation in the Tyler Clementi Foundation Day One anti-bullying campaign in a virtual setting, and board members read portions of the pledge aloud.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board unanimously entered closed session (6-0), reconvened in open session, and unanimously approved the August 27, 2020 personnel report (6-0) before adjourning.

votes.item_title: Approval of August 27, 2020 Monthly Meeting Agenda
votes.notes: Unanimous 6-0 voice vote among the six seated members.
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the August 27, 2020 meeting agenda as presented.

votes.item_title: Approval of June 25 and July 30, 2020 Board Meeting Minutes
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the June 25 and July 30, 2020 meeting minutes.

votes.item_title: Appointment of Frederick Xavier Ravin III to Consolidated District B Board Seat
votes.notes: Unanimous 6-0 appointment vote among all seated members.
votes.discussion_detail: Dr. Mike Lee nominated Frederick Xavier Ravin III to fill the Consolidated District B vacancy left by Xavier Cason's July resignation; nominations required no second and Ravin was appointed unanimously.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Second-Reading Policies (8000 Fiscal Goals, Student Transport, and Community Use of Facilities)
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted redlined second-reading edits to Policy 8000 (Fiscal Goals), the principal emergency student-transport policy, and the Community Use of Facilities policy (Facilitron rentals).

votes.item_title: Adoption of Interim Title IX Policies and Waiver of Second Reading
votes.discussion_detail: Natalie Beyer reluctantly moved and Dr. Mike Lee seconded adopting compromise interim Title IX policies with waiver of second reading to comply with the August 14 Department of Education deadline while pursuing local student protections.

votes.item_title: Adoption of Remote Work Policy on Second Reading
votes.discussion_detail: Adopted the Remote Work Policy on second reading with updates focusing on position eligibility and District efforts to identify alternative assignments.

votes.item_title: Motion to Enter Closed Session
votes.discussion_detail: Entered closed session for the reasons stated on the agenda.

votes.item_title: Approval of August 27, 2020 Personnel Report
votes.discussion_detail: Approved the August 27, 2020 personnel report upon returning from closed session.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Interviews for Consolidated B Seat August 20, 2020 5:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead presided over the August 20, 2020 special interview session of the Durham Public Schools Board of Education to evaluate applicants for the vacant Consolidated District B board seat, with five of six seated members participating live and Matt Sears absent due to an emergency work commitment (committing to review the recording). Nine candidates—Nancy Cox, Luke Deary, Micah Jeter, Antonio Jones, Frederick Xavier Ravin III, Millicent Rogers, Rev. Dr. Fatima Sallie, David Vane, and Chris Wilson—each delivered 10-minute presentations addressing superintendent evaluation metrics, systemic racial equity issues, community engagement, and random draw topics such as student attendance boundaries and pandemic virtual learning. No votes or formal actions were taken during the interview session, with Chair Umstead announcing the board would make its appointment decision at the August 27, 2020 regular meeting.

agenda_items.title: Opening Remarks and Interview Format
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead explained the 10-minute interview format (with three-minute chat warnings by Nicole Smith and a random topic jar) and noted Matt Sears was absent due to an emergency work commitment and would watch the recording and follow up with applicants.

agenda_items.title: Candidate Interview: Nancy Cox
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Former DPS board member (2010-2014) Nancy Cox emphasized using Teacher Working Conditions survey data to evaluate superintendent support, cited middle school free/reduced lunch and hunger disparities, and highlighted her work with Durham Literacy Center, housing committees, and Racial Equity Institute (REI) white caucus.

agenda_items.title: Candidate Interview: Luke Deary
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a brief video camera glitch, Luke Deary discussed his background with open-source principles, high expectations for students and teachers, and proactive funding advocacy rather than waiting on state legislative mandates.

agenda_items.title: Candidate Interview: Micah Jeter
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Lakewood Montessori Middle School parent, educator, and social worker Micah Jeter advocated public education and social justice reform, organizational learning, and strengthening public schools to retain students and federal funding.

agenda_items.title: Candidate Interview: Antonio Jones
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Twenty-year DPS volunteer Antonio Jones stressed culturally relevant curriculum, avoiding tracking or capping students based on zip code, resolving hotspot and remote learning barriers, and building trust with marginalized communities through authentic relationships.

agenda_items.title: Candidate Interview: Frederick Xavier Ravin III
agenda_items.discussion_summary: IT governance and budget development manager, Budget Process Advisory Committee member, and Oak Grove Elementary PTA president Frederick Xavier Ravin III highlighted aligning IT and budget lifecycles, equity-focused policies, mentoring across K-12 and college levels, and early elementary remote learning engagement.

agenda_items.title: Candidate Interview: Millicent Rogers
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Millicent Rogers proposed automated post-service stakeholder surveys correlated with school data in families' chosen languages, empowering teachers with culturally responsive curriculum choices, and meeting communities where they are during school rebuilding and rezoning.

agenda_items.title: Candidate Interview: Rev. Dr. Fatima Sallie
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Rev. Dr. Fatima Sallie outlined three superintendent metrics—graduation rates, recruiting and retaining outstanding teachers of color, and qualitative trust/accountability relationships—while analyzing how disproportionate school discipline interlocks with IEP, EC, and academic access inequities and urging equity-centered boundary decisions.

agenda_items.title: Candidate Interview: David Vane
agenda_items.discussion_summary: David Vane presented a 'ripple effect' evaluation framework centered on contextual community understanding, teacher participation, and parent empowerment, emphasizing that district leadership must bring community genius to the table rather than waiting on Raleigh or Washington.

agenda_items.title: Candidate Interview: Chris Wilson and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Computer scientist and public school alumnus Chris Wilson highlighted mentoring boys of color using former Superintendent Bert L'Homme's community outreach model and drew the random topic of student boundary planning, urging transparent redistricting to relieve severe overcrowding at Githens and Creekside given 1992-era maps and Southwest Durham growth. Chair Umstead closed the interview session and announced the board would decide on the appointment on August 27, 2020.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session August 13, 2020 5:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its nearly six-hour August 13, 2020 work session presided over by Natalie Beyer (with Chair Bettina Umstead joining remotely and participating), the Durham Public Schools Board of Education unanimously approved a formal motion declaring the week of August 17 an Orientation Week to ensure equitable Chromebook and hotspot distribution before academic instruction begins, signed onto a letter requesting federal USDA meal waiver extensions, and adopted a resolution declaring racism a public health crisis. The board also unanimously approved an amended AT&T hotspot consent agreement, waived second reading to temporarily amend Policy 4207 (Directory Information) so teachers could record synchronous lessons for classmates under FERPA, advanced Policy 7503 (Remote Work) to second reading, and waived the Pre-K sliding fee scale during Plan C remote learning. Following sharp debate over a 19% COVID-19 infection rate among school-age youth, employee safety, and health metrics, the board approved opening six DPS Learning Centers by a recorded vote of 5-0-1 (Ayes: Jovonia Lewis, Bettina Umstead, Dr. Mike Lee, Alexandra Valladares, and Natalie Beyer; Abstention: Matt Sears, who cited health and timing concerns, though Board Attorney Rod Malone noted an unexcused abstention legally counts as an affirmative vote). Members also clashed over sending a letter urging Durham PACs to refrain from endorsements in the District B vacancy (with Matt Sears dissenting from the letter as an overstep while Dr. Mike Lee, Natalie Beyer, Jovonia Lewis, and Bettina Umstead supported individual sign-on) and over new federal Title IX regulations (with Dr. Mike Lee opposing compliance unless federal funding was at risk), leading administration to withdraw its waiver request on Title IX after closed session before the board unanimously approved the August 13 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Moment of Silence, Agenda Approval, and July 16, 2020 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Presiding member Natalie Beyer opened with a moment of silence for a recently deceased student and their family. The board unanimously added a Superintendent's Update as Item 6 after public comment and approved both the amended agenda and the July 16, 2020 work session minutes 6-0.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Amended agenda passed 6-0; July 16 minutes passed 6-0

agenda_items.title: General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief Communications Officer Chip Sudderth read one-minute excerpts from approximately 35 submitted public comments (with full texts posted online). Speakers—including teachers, parents, and Durham CAN advocates—urged delaying the August 17 start of instruction due to undelivered Chromebooks, hotspots, and curriculum materials, called for grade-level limits on live screen time, praised the AT&T hotspot expansion, and backed the racism resolution.

agenda_items.title: Superintendent's Update: Orientation Week Delay of Academic Instruction
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Responding to teacher and family concerns over device readiness, Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga and Board Attorney Rod Malone confirmed statutory calendar rules barred moving the August 17 opening date, but principals could dedicate the first week to orientation and relationship building. Jovonia Lewis urged a clear districtwide start date of August 20 for academic instruction, and Dr. Mubenga offered the full first week for orientation and IT testing; Matt Sears moved a formal resolution designating August 17-21 universally as Orientation Week (while giving Dr. Mubenga flexibility with the four early-start specialty high schools), which passed 6-0.

agenda_items.title: USDA Nutrition Waivers Sign-On Letter
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members reviewed a multi-signatory letter to the U.S. Secretary of Agriculture urging extension of federal child nutrition waivers that had expired, warning districts needed meal-delivery flexibility during remote learning. The board voted 6-0 to add DPS as a signatory and post the letter on the district website.

agenda_items.title: Resolution Declaring Racism a Public Health Crisis
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead introduced a resolution brought by Dr. Wanda Boone (Together for Resilient Youth and Durham Committee on the Affairs of Black People), already adopted by Durham County and the City of Durham. Board members took turns reading the full resolution aloud—highlighting structural racism, racial trauma, and equity commitments across leadership, contracting, and policy—before adopting it 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated District B Vacancy Update and PAC Endorsement Letter Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Umstead announced 10 applicants for Xavier Cason's vacated District B seat—Nancy Cox, Luke Derry, Micah Jeter, Antonio Jones, Talisha Joyner, Frederick Ravin, Millicent Rogers, Rev. Dr. Fatima Saleh, David Vennie, and Chris Wilson—and outlined an August 20 virtual interview format featuring a 10-minute speech on board operations, equity, and community engagement plus a two-minute random question. Dr. Mike Lee and Natalie Beyer then proposed a board letter asking local PACs not to endorse in the six-member appointment; Matt Sears opposed the letter as an overstep, and the board opted not to vote, allowing individual members to sign if they wished.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda: AT&T Hotspot Amendment and Academic Contracts
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered a two-item consent agenda consisting of an amended AT&T monthly internet hotspot service agreement and academic contracts. After Natalie Beyer noted inaccurate media coverage and confirmed hotspots for Durham Housing Authority families had never been in question, the board approved the consent agenda 6-0 subject to final attorney review.

agenda_items.title: Policy Updates: 6450, 8000s/9300, Title IX, Policy 4207, and Policy 7503
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni reviewed draft procurement threshold Policy 6450 ($150,000 service bid review), Policy 8000 fiscal goals (sustainability, transparency, equity), Policy 8100 (mandating an annual budget public hearing via 'shall'), Policy 8300 (requiring a new audit firm every four years), Policy 8340 (student transportation in staff vehicles), and Policy 9300 (naming facilities, where Natalie Beyer opposed naming whole schools after individuals). Administration's request to waive second reading on new federal Title IX sexual-harassment rules met sharp resistance from Dr. Mike Lee over weakened student protections and was tabled until after closed session, when Giovanni withdrew the waiver request. The board unanimously waived second reading to adopt a temporary FERPA directory-information amendment to Policy 4207 permitting lesson recordings for classmates, and advanced Policy 7503 (Remote Work) on first reading to August 27.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Policy 4207 passed 6-0; Policy 7503 first reading passed 6-0; Title IX waiver withdrawn

agenda_items.title: Pre-K Sliding Fee Scale Waiver During Plan C
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Superintendent Dr. Nakia Hardy, Dr. Debbie Pittman, and Office of Early Education Director Suzanne Cotterman recommended temporarily waiving the Pre-K sliding tuition scale (which applied to families above 400% of the federal poverty level, or $102,999 for a family of four) while in Plan C remote learning, estimating a quarterly revenue loss of ~$56,207 while NC Pre-K and Durham PreK reimbursements held steady. The board approved the waiver 6-0.

agenda_items.title: DPS Learning Centers Implementation Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Hardy and staff presented a plan with Student U and the DPS Foundation to open six DPS Learning Centers (Eno Valley, Southwest, W.G. Pearson, Githens, Carrington, and Shepard) for 900 students in 1:10 pods (opening August 24 for K-5 and August 31 for 6-12), prioritizing McKinney-Vento/foster students and free/reduced-lunch families with hub busing and an estimated program cost of $486,888 plus $146,000 in custodial/sanitation expenses. Dr. Pascal Mubenga noted school-age youth aged 5-18 accounted for a 19% infection rate, prompting Matt Sears to abstain over safety and timing concerns; after accepting Natalie Beyer's friendly amendment requiring health metrics for opening and closing, the board passed the plan 5-0-1.

agenda_items.title: Follow-Up Items, Closed Session, and August 13 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff summarized action items including tonight's robocall on Orientation Week and integrating health metrics for the Learning Centers. The board entered closed session 6-0, returned at 05:44:27 to unanimously approve the August 13 personnel report 6-0, noted withdrawal of the Title IX waiver request, and adjourned.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Closed session passed 6-0; Personnel report passed 6-0

votes.item_title: Approval of August 13, 2020 Work Session Agenda as Amended
votes.discussion_detail: Dr. Mike Lee moved and Jovonia Lewis seconded approving the work session agenda with a Superintendent's Update added as Item 6. Presiding member Natalie Beyer polled all board members, passing unanimously 6-0.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session August 13, 2020 5:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Letter Urging Local PACs Not to Endorse in District B Vacancy Appointment
disagreements.summary: Board members split over sending a formal letter requesting Durham political action committees refrain from endorsing any of the 10 applicants for the vacant Consolidated District B seat.
disagreements.side_a_position: Encourage local PACs to refrain from endorsements so the six-member appointment process stays transparent and unmuddied.
side_a_arguments: Only six board members vote on the appointment, unlike public elections where endorsements inform voters.
PAC endorsements during a pandemic using virtual meetings could alienate members and replicate issues avoided when PACs refrained during Bettina Umstead's 2019 appointment.
disagreements.side_b_position: Do not issue the letter because an elected body asking PACs not to endorse is an improper overstep.
side_b_arguments: Feedback from PACs during the prior appointment process felt like the school board was overstepping its role by trying to shape independent PAC actions.
disagreements.resolution: Seeing no full board consensus, members agreed not to hold a vote on the letter, leaving individual board members free to sign or decline.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session August 13, 2020 5:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Policy 9300 (Naming Facilities): Allowing Whole Schools to Be Named After Individuals
disagreements.summary: Natalie Beyer objected to draft Policy 9300 language allowing entire school facilities to be named after individuals deceased at least five years, while other members favored keeping the option.
disagreements.side_a_position: Prohibit naming entire schools after individuals altogether.
side_a_arguments: Schools named after people tend to be named after politicians, and prior naming processes (such as Lucas Middle School) proved contentious and difficult.
disagreements.side_b_position: Retain the option to name schools after deceased individuals (at least five years posthumous) when nominated by a sizable or recognizable community group.
side_b_arguments: Durham has rich local history and leadership worth honoring without artificially restricting future naming options.
disagreements.resolution: With Beyer noting she appeared to be the lone objector, administration kept the draft language to return for a full-board vote at the end-of-month meeting.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session August 13, 2020 5:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Federal Title IX Sexual Harassment Policy Waiver and Compliance Risk
disagreements.summary: Board members clashed over administration's request to waive second reading and immediately adopt new federal Title IX regulations taking effect August 14 despite weakened student protections.
disagreements.side_a_position: Refuse to adopt the weakened federal regulations without knowing the concrete penalty for noncompliance.
side_a_arguments: The Trump/DeVos rules raise the bar for pursuing sexual harassment claims, exclude off-campus incidents, and put students and staff at greater risk.
If noncompliance only brings administrative citation rather than loss of federal funding for students and teachers, Durham should stand against the rule.
disagreements.side_b_position: Seek a compliant interim legal path—such as a short-term placeholder resolution—while researching Attorney General Josh Stein's lawsuit and stronger local protections.
side_b_arguments: August 14 is a federal statutory deadline with compliance checks, and the district must avoid jeopardizing federal funds while preserving DPS's internal student-protection practices.
disagreements.resolution: The board tabled the item until after closed session, when Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni withdrew the request to waive second reading and deferred Title IX policies to the next board meeting.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session August 13, 2020 5:00 PM
disagreements.issue: DPS Learning Centers Safety Risks, COVID-19 Spread, and Health Metrics
disagreements.summary: While members recognized urgent equity needs for vulnerable families during Plan C, Matt Sears abstained and others sought strict health metrics before opening six in-person Learning Centers for 900 students.
disagreements.side_a_position: Proceed with launching six DPS Learning Centers on August 24/31 with vulnerable-student prioritization and built-in health metrics for opening and closing.
side_a_arguments: McKinney-Vento, foster, and free/reduced-lunch families urgently need safe supervised spaces, meals, and peer interaction during remote learning.
Embedding epidemiological metrics (inspired by Cambridge Public Schools and Duke/UNC advisors) creates clear guardrails for pausing if community spread worsens.
disagreements.side_b_position: Abstain over unresolved employee and student health risks given a 19% infection rate among school-age youth.
side_b_arguments: Calling the centers a 'guinea pig program,' Sears expressed lack of confidence that August 24/31 was the right or safe moment for employees and children despite strong equity arguments.
disagreements.resolution: Natalie Beyer's friendly amendment requiring health metrics was accepted and the motion passed 5-0-1, with Matt Sears abstaining (counted as an affirmative vote legally).

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Monthly Meeting   July 30, 2020  6:30 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At its July 30, 2020 monthly meeting presided over by Chair Bettina Umstead, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education heard a proposal from Duke/UNC physicians (Drs. Danny Benjamin, Kanecia Zimmerman, Ibukun Kalu/Akinboyo, and Gabriela Maradiaga Panayotti) to establish an NIH-sponsored COVID Scientific Advisory Board providing weekly data synthesis and school-level infection monitoring, with board members unanimously expressing consensus support after Alexandra Valladares pressed for direct clinical and testing benefits for Black and Latinx communities. The board unanimously approved its agenda, a two-item consent agenda (Parkwood Elementary modular classrooms and the Instructure Canvas LMS contract), and the Northern High School design development documents ($84.085M construction estimate within an $85M budget). Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni and Dr. Dietrich/Dr. Bullock presented a September-to-May timeline for convening a 15-20 member Equity Policy Task Force, and Deputy Superintendent Dr. Nakia Hardy delivered a comprehensive operational walkthrough of Plan C remote learning—including synchronous schedules, Wellness Wednesdays, Canvas tutorials, device deployment, and Ignite Online Academy clarity—before the board entered closed session and unanimously approved the July 30 personnel report.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Superintendent's Update: COVID Scientific Advisory Board
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened with a moment of silence honoring the late Rep. John Lewis. Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga noted specialty high schools would begin remotely on August 3 and introduced Duke and UNC pediatricians/epidemiologists proposing an NIH-supported COVID Scientific Advisory Board (ABC Science Collaborative model) serving Durham, Orange, and Chapel Hill-Carrboro districts; after Alexandra Valladares urged ensuring direct community services rather than extractive research, all six board members voiced consensus support.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Approval and General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board approved the agenda 6-0 on a motion by Natalie Beyer and second by Dr. Mike Lee. Chip Sudderth then read five submitted public comments: a teacher criticizing communication limited to English and Spanish, parents questioning how DPS could consider childcare centers while closing schools or rejecting hybrid options, one commenter thanking the board for prioritizing safety, and another criticizing board members and DAE over Plan C and classified-staff childcare ideas; Dr. Mubenga noted translating into many additional languages would cost millions.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda: Parkwood Elementary Modulars and Canvas LMS Contract
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered the consent agenda consisting of a Parkwood Elementary School modular classroom installation contract with MLB Construction Services LLC and a districtwide Learning Management System contract with Instructure (Canvas LMS). Both items passed unanimously 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Equity Policy Development Timeline Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chief of Staff Tanya Giovanni introduced Office of Equity Affairs Executive Director Dr. Bullock, who outlined a timeline to convene a 15-20 member Equity Policy Task Force in September 2020 (including an initial retreat, stakeholder engagement, and policy drafts through April 2021 for May 2021 board review). Board members Jovonia Lewis, Dr. Mike Lee, Natalie Beyer, Alexandra Valladares, Matt Sears, and Bettina Umstead endorsed the timeline, requested built-in accountability and sample reviews of existing policies such as student discipline/appeals, and volunteered for task force participation.

agenda_items.title: Northern High School Design Development Documents
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Under Board Policy 1920, Dr. Julius Monk and Design and Construction Director Frederick Davis presented design development plans and a virtual walkthrough for the new 1,600-student, ~300,000-square-foot Northern High School, estimating construction at $84,085,000 under the $85 million budget cap with wetlands/stream buffers accommodating the three-story core, theater, gym, and CTE wings (culinary, automotive, ROTC, public safety, animal science). After addressing Natalie Beyer's questions on exterior color vibrancy, central kitchen land availability (none usable), and a Roxborough Road GoDurham bus stop, the board unanimously approved moving forward with construction documents.

agenda_items.title: Comprehensive Plan C Remote Learning Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy and academic/student-services directors presented a detailed walkthrough of Plan C remote learning, including 'day-in-the-life' elementary and teacher schedules, synchronous Zoom rotations, Wellness Wednesdays, a Social-Emotional Learning (SEL) hub, Canvas Module Zero digital-literacy support with Durham County Library, the August 3 EC parent information session, and a new Back-to-School web hub. Board members sought clarity on Ignite Online Academy enrollment vs. neighborhood school clustering, daily attendance rules under new DPI guidance, device/hotspot pickup schedules, and preventing high school students with family/work duties from falling through the cracks.

agenda_items.title: Closed Session and July 30, 2020 Personnel Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board voted 6-0 to enter closed session on a motion by Matt Sears and second by Jovonia Lewis. Returning to open session at 03:27:14, the board unanimously approved the July 30, 2020 personnel report as amended on a motion by Natalie Beyer and second by Dr. Mike Lee before adjourning.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Special Meeting   July 23, 2020  5:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At a specially called July 23, 2020 meeting presided over by Chair Bettina Umstead, the Durham Public Schools Board of Education honored former Durham City Board of Education Chair Dr. Beverly Washington Jones and rising seventh-grader Tavian McLean during a moment of silence, unanimously approved its agenda 6-0, and heard one public comment from epidemiologist Dr. Dee Anderson urging strict school-level enforcement of COVID-19 safety protocols. The board then finalized the public process and timeline to fill the Consolidated District B seat vacated by Xavier Cason within the 60-day statutory deadline (September 15, 2020). Members debated the length of the application window (with Natalie Beyer favoring a three-week August 17 deadline due to summer and pandemic disruptions while Dr. Mike Lee and Matt Sears favored a tighter two-week cadence) and interview design (comparing a 7-10 minute prepared speech against individual board-member questions), ultimately reaching verbal consensus on an August 12 application deadline, August 6 question submissions to Chair Umstead, August 13 question review, August 20 interviews, and an August 27 appointment vote.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, Agenda Approval, and Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened with a moment of silence honoring Durham trailblazer Dr. Beverly Washington Jones and Lowe's Grove rising seventh-grader Tavian McLean, lost to gun violence. The board unanimously approved the agenda 6-0 and heard one public comment from Dr. Dee Anderson urging rigorous COVID-19 reopening metrics and uniform school-level compliance.

agenda_items.title: Consolidated District B Vacancy Appointment Process and Timeline
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Using the 2019 District 2 appointment framework, Chair Umstead noted the 60-day statutory deadline of September 15, 2020 and Board of Elections eligibility rules (age 21+ and District B residency) for a term running through 2022. Board members refined the statement-of-interest form—adding equity in education to desired candidate qualities, clarifying daytime hearing commitments, and attaching a District B map—and debated application deadlines and interview formats before reaching verbal consensus on an August 12 filing deadline, August 13 work session review, August 20 virtual interviews, and an August 27 appointment vote.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Special Meeting   July 23, 2020  5:00 PM
disagreements.issue: Application Window Length and Interview Format for Consolidated District B Vacancy
disagreements.summary: Board members differed on whether to provide two or three weeks for District B applications and whether interviews should rely on prepared speeches or per-member live questions.
disagreements.side_a_position: Provide a longer application window (until August 17) and incorporate both individual member questions/spontaneous prompts and prepared speeches.
side_a_arguments: Xavier Cason's resignation surprised the community during summer and the COVID-19 pandemic, warranting extra outreach time.
Allowing each member to ask a question honors board diversity and reveals how candidates think on the fly.
disagreements.side_b_position: Keep a tighter two-week application cadence (August 10) and rely on a 7-10 minute prepared speech covering shared themes to prevent an overly long meeting.
side_b_arguments: Long gaps between filing, interviews, and selection invite excessive lobbying and protracted meetings if 10-13 candidates each answer six separate questions.
disagreements.resolution: Following compromise proposals from Alexandra Valladares and Jovonia Lewis, all six members verbally agreed to set the filing deadline for August 12, submit proposed questions to Chair Umstead by August 6 for thematic synthesis (blending prepared speeches with spontaneous prompts), review the pool on August 13, interview on August 20, and vote on August 27.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Work Session   July 16, 2020  5:00 PM
meetings.executive_summary: At the start of the July 16, 2020 work session presided over by Chair Bettina Umstead, Consolidated District B member Xavier Cason submitted his immediate resignation from the Board of Education after accepting a Director of Community Schools and School Transformation position with the Durham Public Schools Foundation to avoid any potential conflict of interest over future contracts. Following public comments overwhelmingly urging fully remote learning, the six remaining board members unanimously approved the revised 2020-21 year-round calendar, an AT&T hotspot contract (up to $1.65 million for 6,000 devices), and the FY 2019-20 budget closeout and $11.8 million CARES Act spending plan. After reviewing rising Durham COVID-19 cases and 575 employee accommodation requests alongside Governor Roy Cooper's Plan B announcement, board members debated how to address childcare and learning gaps—with Dr. Mike Lee urging community-partner learning spaces while Matt Sears and Alexandra Valladares cautioned against putting classified staff or uncertified personnel into high-risk in-person roles—before voting 6-0 to instruct administration to open the 2020-21 school year under Plan C remote learning for the first nine weeks while exploring community learning spaces.

agenda_items.title: Moment of Silence and Resignation of Board Member Xavier Cason
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead opened with a moment of silence for recent gun violence affecting Durham children. On a point of personal privilege, Xavier Cason announced his immediate resignation after taking a role with the independent DPS Foundation (Director of Community Schools and School Transformation) funded in part by a budgeted DPS match, noting no funds had been transferred and stepping down to avoid future contract conflicts; board members thanked Cason for his integrity and service.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Approval, June 10 Work Session Minutes, and General Public Comment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The six seated members approved the agenda 6-0 and the June 10 work session minutes 6-0 (after Board Attorney Ken Soo advised new members Jovonia Lewis and Alexandra Valladares could vote on prior minutes under Robert's Rules). Chip Sudderth then read excerpts from submitted public comments (with full comments posted online) from teachers, ESL educators, and parents opposing Plan B in-person reopening and calling for Plan C remote learning amid rising COVID-19 cases and the loss of a DPS student.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda: Revised 2020-21 Year-Round School Calendar
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The board considered a single-item consent agenda containing the updated 2020-21 year-round school calendar. Without further debate, the board approved the consent agenda 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Operational Services: AT&T Wi-Fi Hotspot Service Agreement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Julius Monk and IT Director Benjamin Brown presented a negotiated state-contract agreement with AT&T for 6,000 hotspots at $0.99 per device with CIPA filtering, 30 days free service, no activation/cancellation fees, and flexible monthly plans ($20.50/month for 10GB or $30.50/month unlimited plus tax) up to a $1,650,000 cap—significantly undercutting Verizon's $152.24/month quote. Board members questioned Zoom data consumption on 10GB caps, northern Durham coverage, one-hotspot-per-household limits, and Spanish setup guides before approving the contract 6-0.

agenda_items.title: FY 2019-20 Budget Closeout, FY 2020-21 Updates, and CARES Act Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: CFO Paul LeSieur and Alex Modesto reviewed FY20 year-end closeout, state and county budget status, and CARES Act coronavirus relief allocations (~$11.8M) requiring DPI budget setup. Natalie Beyer and Bettina Umstead voiced grave concern over looming state revenue cuts and additional staffing/PPE costs, urging community advocacy to hold ADM enrollment harmless before approving the budget and CARES Act plan 6-0.

agenda_items.title: 2020-21 School Reopening Plan (Plan A/B/C) and Decision to Open in Plan C
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Nakia Hardy, Dr. Julius Monk, and Dr. Pascal Mubenga presented full Plan A, B, and C operational frameworks alongside rising community COVID-19 trends and 575 employee medical/childcare accommodation requests (up from 331 on Sunday). Following debate over Dr. Mike Lee's call for community-partner learning stations versus Matt Sears and Alexandra Valladares's warnings about staffing safety and teacher readiness (citing a DAE survey where only 13% felt ready to return), the board voted 6-0 to instruct administration to open in Plan C for the first nine weeks while exploring safe community learning spaces.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: After Natalie Beyer asked staff to consult high school teachers on synchronous load and Flexible Fridays, the board voted 6-0 to enter closed session. Returning at 04:18:15, the board unanimously approved the July 16, 2020 personnel report 6-0 and adjourned.

disagreements.issue: Creating In-Person Safe Learning Pods/Childcare Under Plan C vs. Staff Safety and Certification
disagreements.summary: While board members united behind Plan C remote learning for the first nine weeks, they diverged over whether DPS should use classified staff or community pods to offer in-person learning spaces for vulnerable students.
disagreements.side_a_position: Pair Plan C remote learning with community-partnered safe spaces/learning stations to protect high-need students who lack safe environments at home.
side_a_arguments: Many low-income and vulnerable students face food insecurity, lack adult supervision, or risk domestic harm under full remote isolation.
Community partners and non-teaching staff or volunteers could help host safe spaces without forcing teachers into classrooms.
disagreements.side_b_position: Caution against relying on classified staff or creating in-person pods that replicate unsafe school exposures and lack certified instructional support.
side_b_arguments: In-person pods recreate the same COVID-19 transmission risks inside high-incidence communities, and classified staff are not certified for instruction.
Only 13% of teachers surveyed by DAE said they felt ready to return, and if flexibility existed, starting after Labor Day would give teachers preparation time.
disagreements.resolution: Board members voted unanimously 6-0 to adopt Plan C for the first nine weeks while directing administration to explore community-partnered safe spaces and bring back concrete health metrics.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Organizational Meeting   July 7, 2020  8:30 AM
meetings.executive_summary: At its July 7, 2020 virtual organizational meeting—opened by outgoing Chair Dr. Mike Lee before newly elected Chair Bettina Umstead assumed the gavel—Judge Rhinehart administered the oaths of office to incoming board members Alexandra Valladares (At-Large) and Jovonia Lewis (Consolidated District A). Under Board Policy 2200, Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga conducted the chair election, unanimously electing Bettina Umstead 6-0 on a nomination by Dr. Mike Lee (with Xavier Cason voting as incumbent District B member prior to his July 16 resignation), and Umstead then presided over the unanimous election of Dr. Mike Lee as Vice Chair. Finally, after Natalie Beyer pushed for weekly Thursday summer meetings and objected to assuming an August 17 in-person opening while Dr. Mike Lee and Dr. Mubenga advocated giving staff downtime between sessions, the board unanimously adopted its 2020-21 meeting schedule adding July 16 and July 30 dates.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Moment of Silence, and Swearing-In of New Board Members
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Outgoing Chair Dr. Mike Lee called the meeting to order and led a moment of silence. Judge Rhinehart administered the virtual oaths of office to newly elected members Alexandra Valladares (At-Large) and Jovonia Lewis (Consolidated District A), both of whom delivered remarks emphasizing equity, student belonging, and community advocacy.

agenda_items.title: Election of Board Chair and Vice Chair
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following Board Policy 2200, Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga opened nominations for Board Chair; Dr. Mike Lee nominated Bettina Umstead, who was elected unanimously by the six other voting members (including incumbent District B member Xavier Cason). Chair Umstead took the gavel and presided over the Vice Chair election, where Dr. Mike Lee was nominated and elected unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Review and Approval of 2020-21 Board Meeting Schedule
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members reviewed the 2020-21 meeting calendar. Natalie Beyer proposed adding weekly Thursday meetings on July 16, 23, 30, and August 6 for COVID-19 reopening updates and objected to assuming schools would reopen on August 17 if unsafe, while Dr. Pascal Mubenga and Dr. Mike Lee supported locking in July 16 and July 30 to allow staff vacation breaks; the board voted unanimously to adopt the schedule with July 16 and July 30 added.

votes.item_title: Election of Bettina Umstead as Board Chair
votes.notes: Xavier Cason voted as incumbent Consolidated District B member prior to his July 16 resignation; nominee Bettina Umstead was not called in the roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: Presiding over the chair election under Policy 2200 (nominations require no second), Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga closed nominations after Dr. Mike Lee nominated Bettina Umstead and polled the six other members, all voting Aye.

votes.item_title: Election of Dr. Mike Lee as Vice Chair
votes.notes: Chair Bettina Umstead presided and announced unanimous election after polling the five other members; Dr. Mike Lee (nominee) was not polled.
votes.discussion_detail: Newly elected Chair Bettina Umstead called for Vice Chair nominations; a board member nominated Dr. Mike Lee (no second required under Policy 2200), and Umstead polled the five non-nominee members, all voting Aye, declaring Dr. Lee elected unanimously.

votes.item_title: Approval of 2020-21 Board Meeting Schedule with July 16 and July 30 Additions
votes.notes: Xavier Cason voted Aye; Chair Bettina Umstead presided and declared unanimous passage.
votes.discussion_detail: Dr. Mike Lee moved and Natalie Beyer seconded adopting the 2020-21 board schedule with July 16 and July 30 added. Chair Bettina Umstead polled the six other members (including Xavier Cason) and declared the calendar passed unanimously.

disagreements.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Board of Education Organizational Meeting   July 7, 2020  8:30 AM
disagreements.issue: Frequency of July/August Reopening Meetings and August 17 Start Messaging
disagreements.summary: Natalie Beyer sought weekly Thursday board meetings through early August and objected to language assuming schools would reopen in person on August 17, while Dr. Mike Lee and Dr. Pascal Mubenga favored fewer fixed dates to give staff respite.
disagreements.side_a_position: Schedule weekly Thursday meetings (July 16, 23, 30, and August 6) and explicitly avoid messaging that schools will reopen in person on August 17.
side_a_arguments: Families and staff are hungry for weekly reopening updates, and current North Carolina COVID-19 conditions are unsafe for in-person school.
disagreements.side_b_position: Lock in July 16 and July 30 meetings while allowing staff vacation downtime and adding special-called meetings only if needed.
side_b_arguments: Central-office staff have been working nonstop on reopening plans and need brief downtime; referring to August 17 merely reflects the current state statutory calendar date pending Governor Cooper's guidance.
disagreements.resolution: The board unanimously adopted the 2020-21 calendar adding July 16 and July 30 while agreeing to call special interim meetings as state guidance evolved.
